title: Complete the square for a simple monic quadratic

source_reference.notes: Original Edexcel 4MA1 Higher-style item for the Year 10 quadratics MVP. Edexcel pivot metadata applied.

problem_text: Write x^2 + 6x + 11 in the form (x + a)^2 + b.

error_category_mapping.diagnostic_sentence: To complete the square, halve the coefficient of x. Half of 6 is 3, not 6.
(x + 3)^2 already includes +9, so compare 11 with 9 to get +2 outside the bracket.

hint_ladder.title: What does completed-square form reveal?
hint_ladder.prompt: You are trying to rewrite the quadratic as one squared bracket plus an outside adjustment. Focus on the coefficient of x.

hint_ladder.title: Pick a starting move
hint_ladder.prompt: Start by halving the coefficient of x to decide what goes inside the bracket. Do not use the full coefficient.

hint_ladder.title: A common slip
hint_ladder.prompt: Many students form the squared bracket but forget that expanding it changes the constant term. The outside number repairs that change.

hint_ladder.title: The general pattern
hint_ladder.prompt: For x^2 + bx + c, use (x + b/2)^2, then adjust the outside constant so the expanded expression would match the original. Apply this pattern; do not copy an example.

expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is halving the x coefficient.
The stuck point is adjusting the constant after forming the square.

mark_scheme_notes: Award 1 mark for (x+3)^2 structure, 1 mark for constant adjustment, 1 mark for correct completed-square form.
examiner_report_notes: Likely errors: using the full x coefficient, no constant adjustment.
metacognition_prompt: Before you start, what kind of form is the question asking you to create?
